text: You're online, researching a specific product. Clicking through sites, maybe adding it to a cart. You just want the best deal. A reasonable goal.
Common wisdom says ads for that product will now follow you everywhere. Every feed, every site, a relentless digital shadow. You brace for the barrage.
But the expected flood of ads never quite arrives, or it fades surprisingly fast. You wonder: did your ad-blocker win? Is the system broken, or did it miss you?
The system didn't miss you; it's optimizing. After a certain point, additional ads have diminishing returns. Your likelihood to click or be persuaded drops sharply.
Showing an ad costs money. Beyond saturation, it's inefficient for advertisers. The system isn't trying to annoy you; it's simply trying to be profitable.
So when intense product research leads to ad quiet, you now understand. It's not a failure, but a calculated decision. The system learned your intent.
